title: Delivery redelivery fee scam
plain_explanation: This uses a common parcel-delivery scam pattern. The fee is kept small so paying feels harmless, but the real goal is capturing your card details on a fake courier page.
safe_action: Do not use the link. Open the courier's official app or website and enter your tracking number yourself.

title: Parcel customs fee scam
plain_explanation: Genuine customs charges are handled through official courier channels with a physical card or tracked notification. Message links demanding customs fees are a common way to capture card details.
safe_action: Check your parcel through the courier's official app or website, typed yourself.

title: HMRC refund scam
plain_explanation: HMRC never texts, emails or WhatsApps about refunds or rebates. Refund messages with links lead to fake GOV.UK-style pages built to capture bank and identity details.
safe_action: Do not use the link. Check your tax position in the HMRC app or on gov.uk, typed yourself.

title: HMRC penalty or arrest threat
plain_explanation: HMRC does not threaten arrest or immediate legal action by phone, text or email. Threat and urgency are pressure tactics to make you pay or share details before you think.
safe_action: Do not reply or pay. If you are worried about your tax, contact HMRC through gov.uk, typed yourself.

title: DVLA vehicle tax scam
trigger_phrases: your vehicle is no longer taxed
plain_explanation: The DVLA does not send payment or refund links by text or email. These messages imitate GOV.UK payment pages to capture card details.
safe_action: Check and pay vehicle tax only on gov.uk, typed yourself.

title: Bank impersonation — suspicious activity
trigger_phrases: a new payee has been added
a new device has been registered
if you did not make this payment call
plain_explanation: Scammers impersonate banks with alarming account alerts to make you tap a link or call their number. Your bank will never mind you hanging up and calling back through 159.
safe_action: Do not use the link or number in the message. Call 159 or use the number on your card, or the app itself.

title: Bank 'safe account' transfer scam
trigger_phrases: transfer your funds to a secure account
protect your money by moving it
your money is at risk, transfer
we have opened a new account for you
plain_explanation: No bank, police force or government body will ever ask you to move money to a 'safe account'. This is always a scam, and the account belongs to the criminal.
safe_action: Stop. Do not transfer anything. Hang up and call 159 to reach your real bank.

title: One-time passcode sharing request
plain_explanation: One-time passcodes exist so that only you can approve actions on your accounts. Anyone asking you to read one out — however official they sound — is trying to get into your account.
safe_action: Never share a security code with anyone. Hang up, then call 159 if it involved your bank.

title: Remote access / tech support scam
trigger_phrases: your ip address has been compromised
allow us to connect to your device
plain_explanation: Genuine companies do not cold-contact people about viruses or ask to connect to your device. Remote-access tools give a stranger full control of your phone or computer and your banking.
safe_action: Do not install anything or call the number. Close the page or hang up — nothing is wrong with your device.

title: Parking QR code scam
plain_explanation: Fake QR stickers are placed over genuine ones on parking machines and signs, leading to convincing payment pages that capture card details. Councils increasingly avoid QR codes entirely.
safe_action: Pay through the operator's own app (such as RingGo or PayByPhone) or a website you type yourself. Check whether the QR sticker looks added on.

title: Winter Fuel Payment scam
plain_explanation: Winter Fuel Payments and cost-of-living support are made automatically or claimed only through gov.uk. Texts inviting you to 'check eligibility' through a link imitate DWP pages to harvest bank details.
safe_action: Do not use the link. Check any support payment on gov.uk, typed yourself.

title: eVisa scam
plain_explanation: Scammers exploit the move to eVisas with fake fee demands and account-update links. Official eVisa services are free to set up and only ever run through gov.uk.
safe_action: Manage your eVisa only through gov.uk, typed yourself. Do not pay fees requested by message.

title: Marketplace off-platform payment scam
trigger_phrases: payment is held until you confirm
send your bank details to receive
plain_explanation: Buyers and sellers are pushed off the marketplace so its protections stop applying. Fake courier, escrow and 'overpayment refund' links are built to capture card or bank details.
safe_action: Keep every payment and message inside the marketplace itself. Never 'verify' through an external courier link.

title: Family emergency / new number scam
trigger_phrases: i need you to pay a bill for me
plain_explanation: The 'Hi Mum/Hi Dad' scam pretends a family member has a new number and urgently needs money. Voice-cloning versions of this scam now exist for calls too.
safe_action: Contact the family member on their usual number, or ask a question only they could answer, before sending anything.

title: Investment or crypto scam
trigger_phrases: our senior broker will call you
plain_explanation: Guaranteed high returns do not exist; that promise is itself the warning sign. Fake platforms show fake profits until you try to withdraw, and 'wallet connection' pages steal crypto directly.
safe_action: Check any firm on the FCA register before investing, and never share a seed phrase with anyone.

title: Recovery fraud (follow-up scam)
trigger_phrases: you have been identified as a victim
processing fee to release your refund
plain_explanation: People who have already lost money are targeted again by fake 'recovery agents' — often the same criminals. Genuine recovery never requires an upfront fee.
safe_action: Do not pay anything to anyone promising recovery. Speak to your bank on 159 and Report Fraud.

title: Job offer fee scam
trigger_phrases: pay for your dbs check through this link
recruitment agent contacted you on whatsapp
plain_explanation: Real employers do not charge fees to start work or recruit through unsolicited WhatsApp messages. Task-based 'earning' schemes take deposits that cannot be withdrawn.
safe_action: Never pay to get a job. Verify the employer independently through their official website.
